newsitem.title: USA: USDA dairy subsidy plan 'a blow to free trade'.
newsitem.headline: USDA dairy subsidy plan 'a blow to free trade'.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand will probably protest against the U.S. Agriculture Department's plan to subsidise exports of U.S. milk, a New Zealand agriculture official said on Tuesday.

"I'll be surprised if it (the protest) hasn't come already," said Brian Chamberlin, a New Zealand agriculture consultant and former president of the Federated Farmers of New Zealand. He added the move was not in the spirit of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
GATT was precursor to the World Trade Organisation.

Chamberlin, who was attending the American Farm Bureau Federation's annual convention, said although the plan was legal under the GATT it would not be in the spirit of trade liberalisation and would hurt non-subsidising countries, including Australia and New Zealand.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman told the convention earlier in the day he would reactivate the Dairy Export Incentive Programme (DEIP) to subsidise sales of milk butterfat and had stepped up DEIP sales for non-fat dry milk.
Glickman said this action was part of a broader USDA programme to increase U.S. milk prices which have fallen sharply in recent months.
"In my view this would affect the United States' credibility," Chamberlin said of the export plan. "It is at the expense of unsubsidised farmers."
